profile.summary: MSA Transformer is a protein language model that reads a whole multiple sequence alignment rather than one sequence. Attention runs twice in each layer, once along the rows (the residues of a sequence) and once down the columns (the same position across the aligned sequences), and training was masked language modelling across many protein families. It is used to embed an alignment, to predict residue contacts from its attention maps, and to score variants zero-shot. It is published inside Meta's ESM repository as ESM-MSA-1b, a 12 layer model of about 100M parameters.

summary_quotes.text: We introduce a protein language model which takes as input a set of sequences in the form of a multiple sequence alignment. The model interleaves row and column attention across the input sequences and is trained with a variant of the masked language modeling objective across many protein families.
MSA Transformer language model. Can be used to extract embeddings from an MSA.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The input is a set of aligned sequences. Each layer applies attention along a row and then down a column, so a residue is informed both by the rest of its own sequence and by what sits at the same alignment position in the family. Training masks residues and predicts them, across many families at once, rather than fitting one model per family. For contact prediction the tied row attention maps are read by a logistic regression, the same method used for the single-sequence ESM models. For variant scoring the repository's program masks each position of the first sequence in the alignment in turn and reads the log probability of each amino acid there, a strategy it calls masked marginals, which is the only strategy it allows for this model.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two checkpoints exist. ESM-MSA-1 was released with the February 2021 preprint. ESM-MSA-1b followed in July 2021 with what the developers call a minor fix in the row positional embeddings, and is the one the README recommends. Both are 12 layers, about 100M parameters, embedding dimension 768, trained on UR50/S with alignments from the 2018_03 release. A result must name which of the two was used, and also the alignment and how deeply it was sampled, because the scoring program takes only the first 400 sequences of the alignment by default.

sections.title: The alignment is part of the input
sections.body: Because the model reads an alignment, the result depends on which sequences are in it and how many. The scoring program reads an a3m file, strips insertions and takes the first n sequences, 400 unless told otherwise. The repository publishes a3m alignments for the structural split dataset, and the README notes that in its own structure comparison the alignment-based methods, ESM-MSA-1 among them, used the trRosetta alignments while the single-sequence models had none.

run_guide.summary: Install the package and score a deep mutational scan with ESM-MSA-1b from an a3m alignment.
prerequisites: PyTorch installed, which the README states as a prerequisite for the repository.
A CUDA GPU: the scoring program moves the tokens to the GPU in the MSA Transformer branch, and the flag to stay on the CPU is --nogpu.
An a3m alignment for the protein, plus a CSV of mutations with a column of mutation names.
About 100M parameters of weights, downloaded automatically into the torch hub cache. The code is MIT; the files read give no separate licence for the weights.

notes: Points for a reviewer. The parameter figure is the README's round 100M; no exact count exists in any file read, so the structured rows carry 100000000. The released dates are month precision (2021-07 and 2021-02) taken from the News list, not full dates. The repository is archived and the GitHub API now answers for facebookresearch/esm as Biohub/esm-archive, so the ownership of the canonical repository is worth a human look; the README, the weight URLs and the pip package name are unchanged. The preprint is CC BY-NC-ND, so store_bytes is false for the Europe PMC record and only the abstract was read; the paper was later published at ICML 2021, which the README notes. This record may overlap an ESM family record, since both draw on the same repository README; the weights, the checkpoint names and the alignment input are specific to this model.
